body.target_estimand: \(\tau_{\omega}(P)=\sum_{k=(g,t)\in\mathcal K}\omega_k E_Q[Y_t(g,1)-Y_t(\infty,1)\mid G=g,S=1]\) for any \(Q\in\mathcal M\) inducing \(P\)

sampling_model.design: Observational staggered adoption in a balanced fixed-\(T\) panel under the OVS target-indexed, period-by-period covariate-conditional one-step DDD parallel-trends restrictions.
sampling_model.units: \((O_i)_{i=1}^n\) are independent and identically distributed panel units.
sampling_model.treatment: Enabling is absorbing through cohort \(G\), and effective treatment requires \(S=1\).
sampling_model.overlap: Every cohort--eligibility cell entering a retained clean comparison has conditional probability at least \(\varepsilon\).
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Fixed-fold cross-fitting estimates cell propensities, outcome-change regressions, and the full shared-cell conditional covariance. A deterministic vanishing eigenvalue threshold selects the conditional contrast rank, Moore--Penrose perturbation derives the loading rate, and either finite-support cell frequencies or a Hölder tensor-spline or wavelet learner supplies the stated covariance rate. Gap inference evaluates explicit directional derivatives on a cross-fitted projected-score sieve.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Theorem 4.1 establishes identification, Theorem 4.2 establishes asymptotic normality, and Remark 4.6 minimizes variance over constant componentwise clean-comparison weights.

Theorem 3.2 derives the covariate-specific optimal efficient influence function and efficiency bound for staggered DiD, while Theorem 4.1 establishes consistency, asymptotic normality, and attainment for the resulting estimator.

Theorem 2 identifies the panel DDD target, Theorem 3 identifies the repeated-cross-section target, Theorem 5 derives the panel efficient influence function, and Theorem 7 derives the repeated-cross-section efficient influence function.
Theorem 5.2 gives variance-minimizing conditional GMM instruments when the conditional covariance is singular and a consistent linear system exists.
Theorem 6.3 derives a fixed-weight stacked-DDD limit law and accounts for dependence from comparison units shared across stacks.
The paper derives an efficient imputation estimator under its event-study model and notes applications to triple-difference designs.
Theorem 3.1 establishes asymptotic linearity and Gaussian approximation for cross-fitted estimators based on orthogonal scores.

body.tldr: The target is a fixed finite aggregate of staggered-DDD group--time effects under the conditional-mean no-anticipation and period-by-period one-step clean-comparison restrictions of Ortiz-Villavicencio and Sant'Anna. The central theorem defines the target, pairwise residual scores, rank, and spectrum entirely from the observed law, proves existence of a compatible full-data extension exactly under the observable clean-comparison equalities, and exhausts the tangent orthocomplement. Conditional generalized least squares then delivers the canonical gradient \(b^{\star}(X)^{\prime}\Psi_P(O)\), including a Moore--Penrose quotient formula for fixed-rank singular covariance. A deterministic foldwise eigenvalue threshold consistently selects the unknown rank, and a perturbation lemma derives the learned loading rate from conditional-covariance learning; fixed-support and Hölder-series regimes make the paper-specific rates concrete. Globally defined Moore--Penrose versions of the published componentwise loading and the best joint constant loading admit an observable projection-residual diagnostic. Exact pointwise equations characterize their efficiency, a bounded binary-covariate family gives the strict gain \(3/512\), and an explicit directional-derivative plus projected-score sieve yields pointwise Wald inference for an observable gap separated from zero.

project_justification.gap: Ortiz-Villavicencio and Sant'Anna (2025, Theorem 4.1, Theorem 4.2, and Remark 4.6) establish identification, pairwise-score asymptotic normality, and constant componentwise GMM optimality but leave semiparametric efficiency in overidentified DDD models open. The closest staggered-DiD efficiency result proves observational equivalence before projecting, and the closest DDD influence-function result is just identified.
project_justification.niche: Eligibility creates simultaneous conditional gap equalities and shared cohort--eligibility histories across targets. These features require a DDD-specific full-data extension, tangent-exhaustion argument, and non-block-diagonal conditional covariance operator.
project_justification.fill: The paper first constructs every target, residual, covariance, rank, and spectrum from observed-law primitives, then proves full-data extendability and exact tangent exhaustion. It next derives the fixed-rank canonical gradient and bound, selects the unknown rank by foldwise thresholding, proves covariance and loading rates in discrete and Hölder-series regimes, constructs an attaining cross-fitted estimator, and gives globally defined comparator loadings with an observable equality diagnostic. The efficiency-gap functional has an explicit pathwise derivative, Moore--Penrose KKT contribution, projected-score sieve implementation, and pointwise Wald limit away from equality.

body.related_work: Ortiz-Villavicencio and Sant'Anna (2025, Theorem 4.1, Theorem 4.2, Remark 4.6, and the conclusion) provide identification under conditional-mean no anticipation and period-by-period one-step DDD parallel trends, pairwise-score asymptotic normality, and the constant within-target GMM benchmark; Theorem 4 of this proposal strictly tightens that benchmark when the pointwise projection equation fails. Chen, Sant'Anna, and Xie (2025, Lemmas 3.1 and 3.2) inform the observable conditional-moment rotation for single-date and staggered DiD, Theorems 3.1 and 3.2 derive the corresponding optimal conditional efficient influence functions and bounds, and Theorem 4.1 establishes consistency, asymptotic normality, and attainment for their estimator. Their DiD model does not supply the DDD-only full-data extension or the tangent-exhaustion proof for coupled eligibility-gap restrictions and shared four-cell histories. Chen and Xie (2026, Sections 2--3 and the full-data extension proofs) clarify why structural identification does not itself establish the observed tangent space. Akbari, Kiyavash, and Ghassami (2025, Theorem 2 for panel identification, Theorem 3 for repeated-cross-section identification, Theorem 5 for the panel efficient influence function, and Theorem 7 for the repeated-cross-section efficient influence function) supply the just-identified reductions; Theorem 11 recovers their panel influence function in the singleton-comparison case. Newey (2001, Theorem 5.2 and its proof) informs the generalized-inverse treatment of redundant conditional moments. Newey (1997) supplies the series-rate and Gram-stability template, while the full shared-cell DDD covariance and thresholded loading rates are established here in discrete and Hölder regimes. Chernozhukov et al. (2018, Theorem 3.1) and Ackerberg et al. (2014) inform the cross-fitting and learned-optimal-weight remainder analysis without being cited as sources of the paper-specific conditional-covariance rates. Hsieh (2026, Section 6) accounts for shared-unit covariance under fixed stacked weights and is a covariance benchmark rather than a target claimed to ignore dependence. Borusyak, Jaravel, and Spiess (2024) obtain efficiency under a different imputation event-study model; no equivalence to the OVS target-indexed conditional DDD model is asserted. The constant-loading CausalSmith parent is internal prior work and is not cited as published evidence.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The early-kill calculation must parameterize the complete finite-support tangent matrix for the binary-\(X\), three-score witness under both conditional clean-cohort equalities. Projection of the aggregate derivative must equal \(b^{\star}(X)^{\prime}\Psi\) in both strata and reproduce \(3/512\). Any additional normal direction, omitted compatibility restriction, or failure of the full-data extension invalidates the canonical-gradient claim and forces a downgrade to conditional score-class optimality.
body.honest_scope: The efficiency theorem is pointwise, uses a fixed finite horizon and target set, and imposes the OVS conditional-mean no-anticipation and target-indexed period-by-period one-step DDD restrictions represented in the observed score system. It does not replace these with almost-sure no anticipation, long-difference parallel trends, or restrictions from untargeted group--time cells. Fixed-rank singularity is covered in the quotient space, and the data estimator recovers that rank with a deterministic threshold under separated positive spectrum; uniform inference when rank changes remains open. The OVS and joint constant comparators use global Moore--Penrose minimum-norm conventions. Gap inference uses a computable projected-score sieve and is stated only for \(\Delta_{\mathrm{cmp}}(P)\ge\delta_0>0\), locally stable comparator KKT ranks, and sieve approximation; inference on the equality boundary remains open. If each target has one clean comparison, the construction reduces to the panel-DDD efficient influence function; if \(X\) is degenerate, it reduces to the best constant joint loading.
